title: Jazzing up the brass band and trumpeter De Jong
summary: No funeral music he remembers, but the brass band played pretty good jazz; he praises a drowned hometown trumpeter named De Jong as very sweet, like Buddy Bolden.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: I wondered, did they ever have music with the funerals like they have here, the brass band?
You don't remember the funerals? No. That brass band, did they ever jazz up any of the numbers? You know, like here they get swinging pretty much out on the street like they do in the dance.

Pretty good jazz, I'll tell you. Thank you, with the brass band, too. That's right. They had some trumpet players in there with my father. It was under the flag. I've heard a man who's trumpet player here. Of course, this man is dead now. Yes. He got drowned. His name was De Jong. Now, what his last name was, I don't know. His name was De Jong.
Same name like Harold De Jong?
Same name, but I don't know his first name, but his name was De Jong.
And he was a trumpet player.
De Jong was about the sweetest trumpet player that anybody wanted. He wanted to hear. Otherwise, De Jong was something like Buddy Bowling. Of course, I don't know Buddy Bowling.
Everybody talks about him. He must have been very great. Very, very great.
